newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs seen steady - lower, pork bellies steady-up.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs seen steady - lower, pork bellies steady-up.

text.p: CME hog futures were expected to open steady to 0.200 cent per lb lower while pork bellies were seen steady to up 0.100, livestock analysts said.

Announced cutbacks in hog slaughter by meatpacker IBP Inc were expected to influence both pork pits again Thursday with hog futures slipping on reduced packer demand and pork bellies to be supported by the planned lighter hog slaughter and ensuing lighter belly production, they said.

Cash hog markets are called steady to lower and should press hog futures. But analysts cited the rise in the latest CME lean index, to 82.50 cents a lb, up 1.33, which narrowed its discount to futures and could provide underlying support.
June lean hog futures Wednesday closed at 83.475 cents a lb.
The cash loin market also held firm and could add to underlying support, they said.
Pork bellies were seen rising on the planned reduction in hog slaughter which would result in tighter fresh belly supplies, they said.
However, some analysts cited further weakness in cash bellies Wednesday which they said showed continued light domestic demand at current price levels.
